title: add-token-stability-scorer-and-retroactive-alert-pause
author: Nikhil Rao
description:
Motivation: Alerts in the token-cost/latency space spike frequently during transient prompt-shape changes and model rollout warmups. This PR introduces a lightweight token stability scorer that summarizes per-invocation token-level variance and a retroactive alert pause (deadzone) that temporarily suppresses alerts for routes showing coherent short-term instability patterns. The goal is to reduce alert noise while preserving signal for true regressions.

What this PR includes: checklist:
- Implement TokenStabilityScorer service that computes a bounded stability score per invocation (range 0..1) based on token latency variance, KV-cache hit patterns, and prefix warmup indicators.
- Add retrospective alert pause controller: when a route's aggregated stability score crosses the instability threshold for a configurable lookback window, the controller adds a short-lived alert mute annotation (retroactive) and emits an explanatory event.
- Dashboard: observability/playgrounds/token-stability-playground.json — a small, interactive panel to visualize scores, token breakdown, and retrospective pauses.
- Telemetry: new metrics token_stability_score (gauge), token_stability_window_pct_unstable (counter), alert_pause_events_total (counter). Metrics include tags: route, model, tenant, region.
- Backfill/compat: safe defaults for previously instrumented paths; scoring is opt-in via alert policy flag.
- Tests: unit tests for scorer heuristics, integration tests exercising simulated warmups via synthetic-replay bench.

Design notes: The scorer is intentionally conservative — it favors precision over recall to avoid masking hard regressions. Score computation is a linear combination of normalized per-token latency variance, kv-cache miss ratio for the invocation, and prefix-change entropy (from existing prompt-shape histograms). Scores are produced at ingestion time and attached to invocation spans and metrics. Retroactive alert pause is applied as an annotation on the alert decision with TTL and audit trail.

Rollout plan: canary 10% of traffic for 48h, watch: alert rate per-route, mean latency, false-suppression metric computed as alerts suppressed but with downstream error increase. Gradual increase to 50% then 100% if synthetic-replay and canary metrics are stable.

Related linear items: ENG-8421 (scorer), ENG-8422 (alert pause), PM-391 (playground). Related investigation: SUP-2345 (customer noise spike from model v12 warmup).

Notes: The description below lists high-level commits, changed areas, and the review conversation. CI flakiness was observed once (integration e2e-observability) and rerun successfully.

review_comments: Aisha K: Can the scorer be configured to ignore synthetic replay traffic? Request: add tag-based opt-out (answered).
Author (Nikhil): Added opt-out flag and unit test for synthetic tag. See commit feat: allow-synthetic-opt-out.
Liam C: Concern: retroactive pause could hide an infra regression if applied globally. Suggest scope to route+model. (updated)
Author (Nikhil): Scope tightened to route+model+tenant; controller rejects pause if global anomaly signals are present.
Sara M: Request adding an audit log line and a metric for suppressed_alert_count. (requested changes)
Author (Nikhil): added alert_pause_events_total and suppressed_alert_count metric; added audit event with owner metadata.
release_notes: Introduce token stability scoring and retroactive alert pause. This reduces noisy alerting for short-lived prompt-shape instability; opt-in via alert policy flag. Metrics: token_stability_score, alert_pause_events_total.
notes_on_rollout: Canary rollout: 10% traffic x 48h -> evaluate alert reduction and suppression-safety signals -> 50% x 72h -> 100% if stable. Automated rollback if suppressed_alert_count > 0.5% of baseline or mean latency increase > 5%.
testing_summary: Unit tests for core heuristics (coverage ~88%), integration tests with replaybench simulated warmups, and a 6h synthetic shadow run against staging with 50k invocations showing 62% reduction in route-level noise and no increase in true error rate. e2e-observability showed transient failure once due to test env flakiness and succeeded on rerun.
